clue.text: Whitehall comedian ignoring answer involving old Scotsman

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the comedian's name
involving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Jack Whitehall is an English stand-up comedian
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A government-district comic snubs a reply and brings in an elderly Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall looks like the seat of government, but it is comedian Jack Whitehall's surname: JACK loses its A, then O goes into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Jock is an informal, sometimes slangy name for any man from Scotland.

clue.text: Competed with Villa playing in claret

indicators.note: a team playing is in action, moving about, so the letters of the club name are moved around
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: claret is a red wine, and its colour is red
the letters of Villa, rearranged

explanation.surface: Aston Villa, playing in their claret shirts, matched their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret and blue are Aston Villa's colours, so the surface is all football; claret just supplies the outer RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival someone is to compete with or equal them, so the past tense matches the phrase.

clue.text: Dishonest Tory leader protected by fishy organisation

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the party name is taken
organisation means arranging things, so the letters of fishy are set in a new order
something protected by another is surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: the letters of fishy, rearranged
the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A shady Conservative chief is shielded by a suspicious outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishy already means suspicious, so it seems to be a synonym, but its letters are the fodder; T goes in before the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty looks evasive and untrustworthy, a near synonym of dishonest.

clue.text: See Dr Who getting prepared and washed

indicators.note: getting something prepared means making it up from raw ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: Watch the Doctor from Doctor Who getting ready and freshening up.
explanation.definitionFit: To shower is to wash under a spray of water, so showered is a past-tense synonym of washed.

clue.text: Alien captain unhappy about everyone getting promoted

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other
in a down clue being promoted means moving up, so the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: sad is a synonym of unhappy
all means every person

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial commander is miserable that all the others are being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Alien is the 1979 film, not a space creature; its ship's captain is called Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ridley Scott's film Alien, Captain Dallas commands the spaceship Nostromo before the creature kills him.

clue.text: Scam inside Las Vegas ends in confusion

indicators.note: ends are the last parts, so only the final letter of each preceding word is kept

blocks.note: the final letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A con game inside Las Vegas ends in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ends seems to belong to Las Vegas alone, but it takes the last letter of all four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of disorder or muddle, a straightforward synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Mean to cover up leg this evening

indicators.note: covering something up means enclosing it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: tight means stingy with money
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide a leg this evening, perhaps under a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean is the miserly sense, not 'intend'. Leg = ON comes from cricket, where the leg side of the field is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is an adverb for during the present or coming evening, the same as this evening.

clue.text: Fooled around, getting angry

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around
heated means agitated or furious

explanation.surface: Someone who fooled around with another partner and the row turned furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Fooled around reads as one phrase meaning had an affair, which is itself a sense of the answer, but around is split off as C.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat someone is to deceive or trick them, so cheated works as a synonym for fooled.

clue.text: Fine artist portraying ladies' fingers

blocks.note: OK means fine or acceptable
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A decent painter depicting women's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies' fingers sounds like a portrait subject, but it is a vegetable name.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are long and slender, which is why the vegetable is also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Parting expressions were translated during trips

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters of were are rearranged
during means within, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: trips and falls are both stumbles
the letters of were, rearranged

explanation.surface: Goodbye phrases were put into another language while travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Trips suggests journeys, which suits the travel picture, but it means tumbles here.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewells are things said on leaving, such as goodbye, so they are expressions used at parting.

clue.text: Driving back 45 inches a long time ago in regret

indicators.note: in places the measure inside the word for regret

blocks.note: to repent is to feel regret
an ell was an old English measure of cloth, 45 inches long

explanation.surface: Pushing back an old length of cloth, someone regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: A long time ago tells you the measure is obsolete; the ell, used for cloth, was 45 inches in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellent describes something that drives back or wards off, as an insect repellent keeps pests away.

clue.text: Extremely sorry — divided by 49 + 50 is just absurd!

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
a word divided by something is split with it in the middle

blocks.note: the first and last letters of sorry
IL is 49 in Roman numerals
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A maths sum interrupting an apology is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: The plus sign just joins the two Roman numerals, IL and L, which together go between S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly means foolish or ridiculous, the same as absurd.

clue.text: Second hospital admits being on strike to make a point

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so a word goes inside the pair of letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
workers on strike are said to be out
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Another hospital lets in staff who are on strike, to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a point sounds like protest, but point is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: South is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Hilton Hotel's plugged by English districts

indicators.note: something plugged by another has it stuck in its middle

blocks.note: Paris Hilton is the hotel heiress and celebrity
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet, plus the S of the possessive
E abbreviates English

explanation.surface: A Hilton hotel is advertised across English areas.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilton Hotel reads as one chain name, but Hilton is Paris Hilton and Hotel is just H.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a small administrative or church district, so parishes are districts.

clue.text: Back in the past, you captured soldiers in time?

indicators.note: a captive is held within, so one piece goes inside the other
going back means running in the opposite direction, so the result is read from the end

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Long ago, you took soldiers prisoner in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: the saying is that time is the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is often called the enemy, as in the phrase 'time is the enemy', because it works against us.

clue.text: In retirement, God's taken to court

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Deus is Latin for God

explanation.surface: A deity in retirement has been sued in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition. Deus is the Latin word for God.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to bring a legal action against them, which means taking them to court.

clue.text: Drunk's wound wants a bit of cleansing

indicators.note: to want something is to lack it, so a letter is missing

blocks.note: wound as in coiled up, not injured
the first letter of cleansing

explanation.surface: A drunk's injury needs some cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind; removing the C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is slang for intoxicated, as in 'well oiled', so it means drunk.

clue.text: Dismissal by Small — success! Starting to get movement with ball

indicators.note: starting points to the start of the next word, its opening letter

blocks.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
S is the abbreviation for small
a win is a success
the first letter of get

explanation.surface: A batsman dismissed by a bowler named Small; success comes as the ball begins to move.
explanation.walkthrough: Small reads as a person's name, like the England bowler Gladstone Small, but it is just S. In cricket outswing is the ball's sideways movement away from the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Outswing is the curving of a bowled cricket ball through the air away from the batsman.

clue.text: Way to inject drugs inducing rush

indicators.note: injecting puts something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: RD abbreviates road, a way
E is ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: A method of injecting drugs that brings on a high.
explanation.walkthrough: Rush looks like a drug high, but it is the plant: the rush and the reed are both tall waterside grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds and rushes are similar marsh plants, and the words are used interchangeably.

clue.text: Firmly lift gold sculpture, luckily hollow

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting moves letters upwards, so they read from bottom to top
a hollow thing has its inside removed, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
the first and last letters of luckily

explanation.surface: Steal a gold statue with force, fortunately empty inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift looks like steal, which fits the heist picture, but it raises OR in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Robustly means in a strong, sturdy, vigorous way, close to firmly.

clue.text: Bond chasing criminal with European in formal evening dress

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are twisted out of order
chasing means coming behind, so this word follows the other

blocks.note: taken as written
E abbreviates European
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond pursues a crook from Europe, both in black-tie evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests 007, but it is just a tie, which goes after the rearranged WITH plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: White tie is the most formal dress code, a tailcoat with a white bow tie, worn at evening events.

clue.text: Allegedly royal seat's in shed

indicators.note: allegedly means as people say, so what is said rather than what is written counts

blocks.note: a throne is the seat of a king or queen

explanation.surface: Supposedly a monarch's throne is kept in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like the garden building but is a past participle, as when a horse sheds or throws its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown off and shed both mean cast off, as a rider is thrown or a skin is shed.

clue.text: Policeman in Boris's first campaign sacking 50

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name
sacking someone removes them, so a letter is thrown out

blocks.note: the first letter of Boris
to lobby is to campaign for a cause
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A police officer in Boris Johnson's early election campaign fires fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby is British slang for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel, founder of the Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby is the traditional British nickname for a police constable.

clue.text: Wallis Simpson finally stops rattling sabre

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the surname
rattling shakes things about, so the letters are jumbled
a stopper plugs a gap, so one letter goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of sabre, rearranged
the last letter of Simpson

explanation.surface: Wallis Simpson finally halts the sabre-rattling.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallis Simpson, the American for whom Edward VIII abdicated, is a false pairing: the definition is Wallis alone, as in Barnes Wallis, the engineer of the bouncing bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnes Wallis was the British engineer who designed the bouncing bomb, so Barnes is the name that goes with Wallis.

clue.text: Poor waiter, beset by official over strong drink

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are put in a different order
over suggests turning something over, so the word is read backwards
beset means surrounded, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a ref, or referee, is a match official
the letters of waiter, rearranged

explanation.surface: A hapless waiter, cornered by an official, over hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is a jocular name for strong spirits such as whisky, because they burn the throat.

clue.text: Split delivered in 4K?

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the expression is taken by its spoken form

blocks.note: the digit and letter, said out loud

explanation.surface: Something split and shipped in ultra-high-definition 4K.
explanation.walkthrough: 4K looks like a screen resolution; spoken, it is the number four and the letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: A fork is a place where a road or branch divides, and to fork is to split in two.

clue.text: Cleaner scrubs overalls after pocketing tips

indicators.note: tips are the ends of things, here the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A cleaner scrubs a pair of overalls after emptying gratuities from the pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: Tips looks like money in the pockets, but it signals the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a cleaning agent, so it is a cleaner in the sense of the substance used.

clue.text: God taking part in horse race coming up

indicators.note: taking part in means being part of, so the answer is a part of the following words
in a down clue coming up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A god joins a horse race and comes up on the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, the counterpart of the Roman Mars.

clue.text: Escort partners inside gathering

indicators.note: inside places the partners within the word for escort

blocks.note: to bring someone is to escort them along
East and West are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: An escort has partners inside the gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and West play as a partnership, so partners can be EW (or NS).
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering as in a storm gathering: something brewing is building up and about to break.

clue.text: Will I punch social workers in the guts?

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so these letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: worker bees are social insects
'll is the short form of will, as in I'll
taken as written

explanation.surface: Will I hit the social workers in the stomach?
explanation.walkthrough: Social workers looks like a profession, but it is bees, the classic social insects with a worker caste.
explanation.definitionFit: Belly and guts both refer to the stomach or abdomen, so bellies matches guts.
